The problem

In an emergency, time is lost looking for information.

When someone collapses, responders need to know who they are treating and where the nearest help is. Today that information is scattered, or locked away with a patient who cannot speak.

7–10%lower chance of survival for every minute without CPR and defibrillationAmerican Heart Association
32%of emergency department visits have incomplete patient information, delaying careStiell et al., CMAJ 2003, 1,002 visits
8%of people leave hospital alive after a cardiac arrest outside hospital in EuropeEuReCa TWO study, 28 countries

Live map

Risk assessment

A score for how prepared you are for an emergency, and the next step to improve it.

  • Critical record
  • Reachability
  • Release policy
  • Live signals
04 / 05

Emergency QR

A time-limited code a clinician can scan. It carries a token, never your clinical data.

  • Expires in 2 minutes
  • You choose what is released
  • Every scan is logged
Expires in 2:00
